hero.headline: FBI stops potential explosive drone attack on White House UFC event
hero.body:
Federal authorities disrupted a potential attack targeting the UFC Freedom 250 event at the White House, FBI Director Kash Patel announced Tuesday. The operation spanned multiple states and resulted in several arrests.

Law enforcement first learned of the threat on June 10 through encrypted communications on Signal, just days before the sporting event took place on the White House South Lawn. Patel's statement confirmed that the plot involved explosive-laden drones aimed at the outdoor UFC competition.

The Secret Service and FBI coordinated the security response across multiple jurisdictions to track down those allegedly involved in planning the attack. Federal agents monitoring encrypted messaging detected discussions about the potential threat and moved quickly to identify and apprehend suspects before the event occurred.

Patel did not provide specific numbers of arrests or identify the individuals involved in the alleged plot. The investigation did not disclose whether authorities seized any actual explosives or drones, or what additional security measures were implemented at the White House after the threat was discovered.

The UFC Freedom 250 event marked an unusual use of the White House grounds, which are traditionally reserved for state dinners, diplomatic ceremonies, and ceremonial events. The competition drew thousands of attendees to the South Lawn, one of the most heavily protected sites in the United States.

The incident highlights security challenges posed by large public gatherings at sensitive government locations. The discovery of the threat raises questions about how federal agencies monitor and respond to potential dangers targeting major events held at the nation's capital.

Dana White, the UFC's president, later stated the White House event would be a one-time occurrence. He cited weather concerns, the logistical complexity of constructing a cage and staging infrastructure at a federal landmark, and the substantial costs associated with holding the event at the presidential residence as reasons why such events would not be repeated.

The successful interdiction demonstrates the ongoing role of encrypted message monitoring in detecting potential threats to major public events. The operation reflects broader security protocols for protecting high-profile gatherings, particularly those held at locations with symbolic and strategic importance to the federal government.

The incident occurred amid a broader period of scrutiny over security protocols and threat detection at sensitive venues. While details about the specific nature of the threat and those arrested remain limited, the operation underscores the coordination required between multiple federal agencies to protect events drawing large crowds to prominent government sites.

cards.headline: Ukraine strikes major Moscow oil refinery as G7 leaders meet
cards.body:
Ukrainian drones struck a major oil refinery in the Moscow region, located 15 kilometers from the Kremlin, marking a significant attack on Russian energy infrastructure. The strike targeted facilities used for fuel supply and energy exports at a critical moment in diplomatic efforts to end the war.

The timing of the attack coincides with ongoing peace negotiations. Ukraine and Russia concluded a second round of US-brokered talks in Abu Dhabi on Thursday, conducting a major prisoner swap and agreeing to resume negotiations soon. However, Donald Trump's special envoy Steve Witkoff cautioned that "significant work remains" in the weeks ahead, tempering expectations of a swift resolution to Europe's biggest conflict since World War II.

The meetings represented the most substantive engagement between senior delegations from Kyiv and Moscow in months, suggesting a tentative revival of diplomatic efforts nearly four years into the war. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy described the trilateral talks with the United States and Russia as "not easy" but said Ukraine would remain constructive and seek a fair deal to end Russian aggression. Kyrylo Budanov, head of Ukraine's presidential office, called the negotiations "genuinely constructive" and thanked the United States and United Arab Emirates for mediating.

Russia's representative, Kirill Dmitriev, also struck a positive note, reporting progress and "forward movement" in discussions on ending the war. Russia separately signaled readiness to engage with more European leaders, saying it could "listen to any proposal" if it considered it a serious attempt to reopen diplomatic channels.

Western sanctions continue to pressure Russia's economy. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said more American sanctions against Russia would depend on the progress of peace talks. He indicated he would consider new sanctions against Russia's shadow fleet, a step the Trump administration has not taken since returning to office in January 2025. Bessent credited existing sanctions against Russian oil companies Rosneft and Lukoil with helping bring Russia to the negotiating table.

The European Union's sanctions envoy David O'Sullivan said sanctions were having "significant impact" on the Russian economy, though not a complete solution. He expressed confidence that after four years of sanctions, their effects were clear, noting that "we may be, in the course of 2026, coming to a point where the whole thing becomes unsustainable" due to distortions in Russia's war economy.

The Russian economy faces its greatest strain since the early days of the invasion, with oil revenues plummeting, inflation running at about 6 percent, and interest rates at 16 percent.

Meanwhile, night-time shelling by Ukrainian forces inflicted "serious damage" in the Russian city of Belgorod near the border, according to the region's governor. Power was cut in some districts of the city, which lies about 40 kilometers from the Ukrainian border.

cards.headline: Senate Republicans demand more details on Trump Iran peace deal
cards.teaser: Republican senators are holding back from endorsing the announced peace agreement with Iran, saying they need more information about whether it stops Iran's nuclear program.
cards.body:
Republican senators are withholding judgment on President Trump's announced Iran peace deal, saying they need additional information before weighing in. Members from both parties agreed that Congress must receive more details soon.

Trump's allies on Capitol Hill want clarity on whether the agreement would curb Iran's nuclear program, citing concerns that prompted U.S. and Israeli strikes against Iran earlier this year. Senators are seeking assurances that any deal addresses the core issues that led to the military action.

cards.headline: Iran war could reshape Republican standing with voters
cards.teaser: The brief U.S.-Iran war stands to have larger consequences for the GOP with voters, though the truce scheduled for Friday has not yet been finalized.
cards.body:
The brief war between the United States and Iran could carry significant consequences for Republicans with voters, even as questions remain about whether the truce will hold. President Trump and Iranian leaders are known for unpredictable negotiating styles, leaving uncertainty about whether the agreement will be signed Friday as announced.

Assuming the deal holds, the conflict will be remembered as brief, but its political impact on the Republican Party may extend well beyond the short duration of hostilities. The outcome of negotiations and the terms of any final agreement will shape how voters assess the administration's handling of the crisis.

cards.headline: Oil Prices Fall as Markets React to US-Iran Agreement
cards.teaser: Oil prices continued dropping as traders assessed the implications of the preliminary agreement between the United States and Iran.
cards.body:
Oil prices have fallen following the announcement of a preliminary US-Iran agreement. As part of the deal, the Strait of Hormuz waterway will be reopened, according to President Donald Trump. The prospect of Iranian oil returning to global markets has prompted energy traders to reassess their positions.

However, gas prices at the pump may not decline immediately. Damaged infrastructure in the region and risks associated with transporting energy could sustain higher fuel costs despite the agreement. Experts suggest that elevated prices for gasoline, groceries, and flights will persist beyond the current geopolitical tensions.

cards.headline: Iran says deal with US requires Israeli withdrawal from Lebanon
cards.teaser: Iranian officials stated that any agreement to end the conflict with the United States must include the removal of Israeli forces from Lebanon.
cards.body:
Iran announced that its negotiations with the United States include a requirement for Israeli forces to leave Lebanon as part of any deal to end the war. Iranian Foreign Minister indicated that the next round of talks with US officials will begin on Friday. Iranian state television reported that an official said the end of the war includes ending Israel's presence in Lebanon.

President Donald Trump commented on the situation, saying Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu must be more responsible regarding Lebanon. Trump also warned that if Israel cannot complete its objectives, Syria should take action. The negotiations represent ongoing efforts to resolve the broader regional conflict that has involved multiple countries.

cards.headline: Air Force B-52 bomber crashes at Edwards Air Force Base, killing eight crew members
cards.body:
An Air Force B-52 Stratofortress crashed shortly after takeoff at Edwards Air Force Base in California's Mojave Desert on Monday morning, killing all eight people aboard. The aircraft went down at approximately 11:20 a.m. during what officials described as a routine test mission.

Edwards Air Force Base confirmed the incident in a statement, noting that initial indications suggest the crash was not survivable. Emergency response personnel responded to the scene immediately, and officials worked to account for all personnel involved.

The B-52 Stratofortress is a long-range strategic bomber that has served the Air Force for decades. While the aircraft typically operates with a crew of five, specific configurations can vary based on mission requirements. The base has not yet released the names or details of those killed in the crash.

Edwards Air Force Base functions as a test facility for military aircraft and serves as home to the Air Force Test Center. The installation has played a significant role in aviation history, having previously served as a landing site for the Space Shuttle program and hosting numerous aircraft flight test operations.

The cause of the crash remains under investigation. The Air Force typically grounds similar aircraft following major incidents while safety reviews are completed. Federal investigators will examine the circumstances surrounding the crash to determine what led to the aircraft going down.

This incident represents one of the deadliest Air Force crashes in recent years. The B-52 fleet has remained in continuous service since the 1950s, with ongoing modernization efforts designed to extend the aircraft's operational life well into the future. The aircraft remains a critical component of the Air Force's strategic capabilities, supporting long-range strike missions and maritime operations.

The loss of eight crew members marks a significant tragedy for the Air Force and the families of those killed. The service has faced challenging circumstances in recent months, including other military personnel losses. In February, the Air Force conducted a dignified transfer at Dover Air Force Base for service members killed in action overseas.

The Air Force has not announced any immediate operational changes to the B-52 fleet, though safety reviews following the Edwards crash typically result in temporary groundings of similar aircraft. The investigation into Monday's crash will likely take several weeks as officials work to recover and analyze evidence from the accident site.

Edwards Air Force Base will continue normal operations while the investigation proceeds. The base will likely release additional information about the incident as the investigation develops and families of the crew members are notified.

cards.headline: Two men convicted in arson attacks targeting UK Prime Minister Starmer
cards.teaser: A court found two men guilty of setting fire to properties linked to British Prime Minister Keir Starmer, in attacks that originated from Russian direction.
cards.body:
Two men have been convicted of arson attacks on properties connected to UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer in 2025. Prime Minister Starmer expressed that he was "very pleased for my family's sake" following the convictions, saying justice has been done.

The investigation revealed that a Russian-speaking handler coordinated the attacks but escaped before authorities could apprehend them.

cards.headline: Cuba tourism drops 58 percent under US pressure campaign
cards.teaser: Foreign visitors to Cuba have declined sharply compared to last year as sanctions and oil restrictions take effect.
cards.body:
Foreign visitor numbers to Cuba have plummeted 58 percent year-over-year, according to Cuban officials. The sharp decline coincides with intensified US sanctions and restrictions on oil supplies to the island nation.

Tourism represents a critical economic lifeline for Cuba, generating substantial foreign currency and employment. The combined impact of sanctions and the effective oil blockade has dealt a severe blow to an economy heavily dependent on international visitors.

cards.headline: Russian artist and Putin critic shot dead in Poland
cards.teaser: Robert Kuzovkov, a Russian artist known for his political caricatures, was killed in Poland.
cards.body:
Robert Kuzovkov, known by the pseudonym Semyon Skrepetsky, was shot dead in the eastern Polish town of Biała Podlaska. The Russian artist was known for creating political caricatures, including depictions of Vladimir Putin.

According to Polish prosecutors, five shots were fired at Kuzovkov during the attack on Monday, with one shot to the head. Two Belarusians have been detained in connection with the killing.

cards.headline: India temporarily bans Telegram over exam paper leak concerns
cards.teaser: The Indian government blocked Telegram after allegations that the messaging app was used to leak national exam papers.
cards.body:
India has temporarily banned Telegram following concerns about exam fraud. The messaging platform's restriction will remain in effect until June 22. Authorities also required the app's message editing feature to be disabled as part of the enforcement measures.

The ban came after the NEET medical entrance examination was cancelled due to allegations that exam papers had been leaked. The scandal sparked widespread protests across the country, raising questions about the integrity of India's examination system.

cards.headline: Nigerian army rescues widow of general who died in captivity
cards.teaser: Military forces freed Amina Abubakar, whose husband died while being held by kidnappers in northwest Nigeria.
cards.body:
The Nigerian army has rescued Amina Abubakar, whose husband Major General Rabe Abubakar died while being held captive. The couple were abducted together in northwest Nigeria at the end of last month.

The kidnapping occurred in a region plagued by armed groups who target civilians and former security officials for ransom. The military launched operations to locate and free those being held by the kidnappers.

cards.headline: Tropical storm watches expected as flooding threat develops across Gulf Coast
cards.teaser: A tropical disturbance in the Gulf of Mexico could bring catastrophic flooding to parts of the South as watches are anticipated within hours.
cards.body:
A waterlogged tropical disturbance in the Gulf of Mexico is expected to bring flooding to parts of the South, with tropical storm watches likely to be issued soon. The system, designated Invest 90-L, could develop into Tropical Storm Arthur along the Texas Gulf Coast.

The weather system poses a major flood threat extending from Texas into Louisiana and the Deep South. Forecasters warn of a multi-day tropical rainfall event that could produce catastrophic flooding across the region. Texas faces an immediate threat, with alerts potentially coming within hours.

cards.headline: Pennsylvania issues quarantine order as screwworm cases spread in United States
cards.teaser: Pennsylvania issued a quarantine order after New World screwworm cases were confirmed in the country, with infestations rising to 12 in Texas.
cards.body:
Pennsylvania has issued a quarantine order following confirmation of New World screwworm cases in the United States. The parasite infestations have risen to 12 cases as the pest spreads in Texas, according to Texas Public Radio.

The New World screwworm is a parasite that poses risks to livestock and outdoor pets. Texas Farm Bureau launched free inspector training programs to help identify and manage the infestations. Officials have provided guidance on how to protect outdoor pets from the parasite as containment efforts continue.

cards.headline: Rental market offers move-in deals in some regions amid apartment construction boom
cards.teaser: About 40 percent of rentals on Zillow now offer move-in incentives as a construction surge creates an apartment surplus in parts of the country.
cards.body:
About 40 percent of rentals listed on Zillow are offering move-in deals, including offers like a month of free rent, as landlords compete for tenants. The incentives stem from a construction boom that has created an apartment surplus in some parts of the United States.

Whether renters benefit from the current market depends on their location. The construction surge has affected different regions unevenly, with some areas experiencing significant increases in available units while others remain tight. The move-in deals represent an effort by landlords to fill newly constructed units in markets with increased supply.

cards.headline: Serena and Venus Williams receive Wimbledon doubles wildcard
cards.teaser: Serena Williams will play alongside her sister Venus in the Wimbledon women's doubles after receiving a wildcard entry.
cards.body:
Serena Williams has been granted a wildcard to compete in the Wimbledon women's doubles with her sister Venus. The announcement marks a significant moment as Serena returns to competition after four years away from professional tennis.

The Williams sisters have a storied history at the All England Club, having won six doubles titles together at Wimbledon. Neither player requested a singles wildcard for the tournament. Venus, who turns 46 on Wednesday, has remained active on tour since her 1994 debut, while Serena, a seven-time singles champion, has not indicated plans to return to singles competition.

cards.headline: Trump questions whether Georgia Senate candidate can win with abortion position
cards.teaser: Former President Trump raised concerns about Representative Mike Collins's ability to win the Georgia Senate race given his stance on abortion.
cards.body:
Former President Trump questioned whether Representative Mike Collins could win the Georgia Senate race due to his abortion stance, according to Politico. Despite his concerns, Trump issued a last-minute endorsement of Collins in the high-stakes race.

The Georgia Senate race has drawn national attention as Republicans work to maintain or expand their position in the chamber. Collins received Trump's endorsement despite the former president's reservations about how the candidate's abortion position might affect his electability in the state.

cards.headline: World Cup draws large crowds as fans spend heavily on tickets and travel
cards.teaser: Fans in the United States, Canada, and Mexico are spending significant amounts on World Cup tickets, transportation, and accommodations.
cards.body:
Fans attending the World Cup across the United States, Canada, and Mexico are making significant financial commitments for tickets, transportation, and accommodation. While some describe the costs as steep—with one fan calling it "daylight robbery"—many believe the experience justifies the expense.

The tournament has generated strong enthusiasm across all three host nations as matches get underway. The competitive opening games have attracted fans willing to pay premium prices for the opportunity to attend matches in person.

hero.headline: SpaceX Acquires AI Coding Startup Cursor for $60 Billion
hero.body:
SpaceX has agreed to acquire Anysphere, the company behind the Cursor AI coding assistant, for $60 billion in stock. The deal comes just days after SpaceX completed its initial public offering, which valued the space and technology company at over $2 trillion. The acquisition marks one of the largest technology deals in recent years and signals SpaceX's expansion into enterprise software.

Cursor has gained popularity as an AI-powered coding tool that helps software developers write and edit code more efficiently. The platform integrates artificial intelligence to suggest code completions, identify bugs, and automate routine programming tasks. Industry observers had noted Cursor's relationship with AI research company Anthropic, though the exact nature of that partnership remains unclear.

The transaction will be paid entirely in SpaceX stock, allowing Anysphere shareholders to participate in the newly public company's growth. SpaceX shares have surged more than 50 percent across three trading sessions since the company went public, pushing its market capitalization close to $2.75 trillion. The stock continued rallying in premarket trading, nearing levels that would bring SpaceX within range of Microsoft's market value.

The acquisition positions SpaceX to compete in the enterprise software market, where AI coding tools have become increasingly valuable to technology companies seeking to improve developer productivity. Major technology firms have invested heavily in similar tools, viewing AI-assisted software development as a key growth area. By bringing Cursor's technology in-house, SpaceX gains capabilities that could support its own engineering operations while also creating a new business line.

The deal's size reflects both the high valuations currently commanded by artificial intelligence companies and SpaceX's ambitions beyond its core aerospace business. The $60 billion price tag represents a substantial bet on the future of AI-powered software development tools and their potential to transform how code is written across industries.

cards.headline: Fox Acquires Roku in $22 Billion Streaming Deal
cards.teaser: Fox has agreed to buy streaming platform Roku, joining the competition for control of television viewing.
cards.body:
Fox Corporation has acquired Roku for $22 billion, uniting the media company with the popular streaming platform. The deal reflects a strategic shift in the industry as traditional television audiences migrate online. Fox now controls both content and the hardware and software platform through which millions of viewers access programming.

The acquisition positions Fox to compete with other media companies for dominance in the streaming market. By combining Roku's platform with its news and sports offerings, Fox is betting that integrating streaming services will strengthen its position as television consumption continues moving away from cable toward online viewing.

cards.headline: Oil Prices Fall as Markets React to US-Iran Agreement
cards.teaser: Oil prices continued dropping as traders assessed the implications of the preliminary agreement between the United States and Iran.
cards.body:
Oil prices have fallen following the announcement of a preliminary US-Iran agreement. As part of the deal, the Strait of Hormuz waterway will be reopened, according to President Donald Trump. The prospect of Iranian oil returning to global markets has prompted energy traders to reassess their positions.

However, gas prices at the pump may not decline immediately. Damaged infrastructure in the region and risks associated with transporting energy could sustain higher fuel costs despite the agreement. Experts suggest that elevated prices for gasoline, groceries, and flights will persist beyond the current geopolitical tensions.

cards.headline: Kevin Warsh Opens First Federal Reserve Meeting as Chairman
cards.teaser: The new Federal Reserve chairman faces questions about interest rates, inflation and central bank independence at his first policy meeting.
cards.body:
Kevin Warsh is presiding over his first Federal Reserve policy meeting as chairman. The central bank faces significant challenges including persistent inflation and questions about future policy direction. Some policymakers may consider rate increases rather than the cuts that were previously anticipated.

Warsh has signaled a preference for less frequent Federal Reserve communication, a shift that could result in more market surprises compared to recent practice. Interest rate policy, inflation management and the Fed's independence are key issues facing the new chairman as financial markets monitor the central bank's direction under his leadership.

cards.headline: General Motors in Talks to Supply Weapons Components to Lockheed Martin
cards.teaser: The automaker is negotiating a deal to manufacture parts for defense contractor Lockheed Martin's weapons systems.
cards.body:
General Motors is in discussions with Lockheed Martin to supply components for weapons production, according to Wall Street Journal reporting. The potential partnership would expand GM's manufacturing operations into the defense industry supply chain.

Defense contractors are seeking additional manufacturing capacity and suppliers with advanced production capabilities. GM's industrial scale and manufacturing expertise position it to support Lockheed Martin's weapons programs.

cards.headline: Gas Prices Expected to Remain Elevated Despite Iran Deal
cards.teaser: Industry experts say the US-Iran agreement may not quickly reduce prices at the pump due to infrastructure damage and transportation risks.
cards.body:
Gasoline prices are unlikely to drop immediately following the preliminary US-Iran agreement, according to energy analysts. Damaged oil infrastructure in Iran and risks associated with transporting crude from the region could sustain higher costs in the near term.

The conflict's disruption to Middle Eastern energy production and transportation has had lasting effects on fuel costs. While the agreement includes reopening the Strait of Hormuz waterway, markets will need time to adjust to the new diplomatic situation before consumers see relief at the pump.

cards.headline: UK Government Objects to Thames Water Rescue Plan
cards.teaser: The environment secretary says the proposed deal for the struggling utility does not adequately protect consumers or environmental interests.
cards.body:
The British government has objected to a proposed rescue deal for Thames Water, moving the utility company closer to potential nationalization. Environment Secretary officials said the agreement fails to provide sufficient protections for consumers and the environment.

Thames Water has been seeking a financial restructuring as it struggles with debt and infrastructure needs. The government's rejection of the current proposal leaves the company's future uncertain and raises the possibility of public ownership. The utility serves millions of customers in London and surrounding areas.

hero.headline: SpaceX to acquire Cursor for $60 billion in stock following IPO
hero.body:
SpaceX announced it will acquire Cursor for $60 billion in an all-stock deal, capitalizing on momentum from its record-breaking initial public offering. The acquisition is designed to strengthen SpaceX's artificial intelligence operations, which the company has identified as a key growth area.

The move comes days after SpaceX completed what has been called the largest IPO in history. The company began trading on Friday at $150 per share, well above its pre-offer price of $135. Investor enthusiasm drove the stock higher throughout the day, closing at $160 and valuing the company at $2.1 trillion. The IPO ultimately raised $85.7 billion after underwriters exercised their full option to purchase additional shares.

During its IPO roadshow, SpaceX highlighted artificial intelligence as a significant opportunity, citing a $26 trillion addressable market. The Cursor acquisition represents a major bet on capturing enterprise customers and closing gaps with competitors like OpenAI and Anthropic.

Elon Musk, SpaceX's founder and CEO, holds roughly 85 percent of the company's voting shares. The IPO made him the world's first trillionaire, with his net worth reaching $1.1 trillion according to Forbes. At SpaceX headquarters Friday morning, Musk emphasized the company's long-term vision. "It is certainly hard to believe that a little company that started in a warehouse in El Segundo is now going public with the largest IPO ever," he said.

SpaceX's president, Gwynne Shotwell, announced the milestone from the Nasdaq trading floor in New York, where Elton John's "Rocket Man" played as executives rang the opening bell. She noted that SpaceX had launched a Falcon 9 rocket that same morning from Cape Canaveral, carrying 29 Starlink satellites into orbit.

The company has structured itself as a conglomeration of several businesses, including satellite provider and internet service company Starlink, the AI startup xAI, social media platform X, and its core rocket business. However, SpaceX is not yet profitable. Last year the company generated $18.7 billion in revenue while recording a $4.3 billion operating loss.

The Cursor acquisition will be paid entirely in SpaceX stock rather than cash, preserving the company's reserves for ongoing rocket development and satellite deployment. The deal requires regulatory approval and is expected to close within coming months. The company has not disclosed detailed plans for integrating Cursor's technology or team into its existing AI operations.

The timing of the acquisition immediately following the IPO suggests SpaceX planned to use newly issued public shares as acquisition currency, allowing the company to pursue major strategic goals without depleting cash reserves needed for core operations.

cards.headline: ChatGPT's market share falls below 50% for first time
cards.teaser: The AI chatbot remains the most popular assistant globally but now holds less than half the total market.
cards.body:
ChatGPT's market share has dropped below 50% for the first time, marking a significant shift in the AI assistant landscape. Despite this decline, the platform remains the dominant player with over 1.1 billion monthly users worldwide.

The competition is intensifying as other platforms gain ground. Gemini holds the second position with 662 million monthly users, while Claude captures 245 million users. This distribution shows how the AI assistant market is becoming increasingly fragmented as users explore alternatives.

cards.headline: India bans Telegram temporarily over exam fraud concerns
cards.teaser: The government imposed restrictions on the messaging app until June 22 and ordered the message editing feature disabled.
cards.body:
India has temporarily banned Telegram nationwide until June 22 due to concerns that the messaging app facilitates exam fraud. The government cited the platform's message editing feature as a particular problem, as it allows users to modify messages after they've been sent—a capability authorities believe enables cheating during examinations.

As part of the restrictions, Telegram has been required to disable its message editing functionality. The ban represents a significant move by Indian authorities to combat fraudulent activity in the education sector.

cards.headline: Threads reaches 500 million monthly users, adds personalization tools
cards.teaser: Meta's social platform introduced new features including an algorithmic control tool for users.
cards.body:
Threads has reached 500 million monthly active users, the Meta-owned platform announced today. The milestone comes as the social network rolls out new features aimed at enhancing user control and community engagement.

Among the launches is a "Your Algo" tool that gives users greater control over their feed content. These personalization and community features represent Threads' continued efforts to expand its capabilities as it competes in the social media landscape.

cards.headline: Foundation Alloy raises $22 million to scale metal production technology
cards.teaser: The startup uses mechanical beating instead of heat to create alloys for military, luxury, and culinary applications.
cards.body:
Foundation Alloy secured $22 million in funding to expand production of metals created through a novel manufacturing process. The startup produces alloys by mechanically beating metals rather than heating them, which it claims produces materials suitable for military drones, luxury watches, and chef's knives.

The company plans to use the funding to scale up production capacity for its alloys. Foundation Alloy's mechanical process represents a departure from traditional metallurgy techniques that rely on heat treatment to combine and strengthen metals.

cards.headline: Malaysian messaging startup Respond.io raises $62.5 million
cards.teaser: The company uses AI agents to handle customer inquiries and charges per conversation rather than per user seat.
cards.body:
Respond.io, a Malaysian messaging platform, raised $62.5 million in funding. The company plans to use the capital to pursue acquisitions as it expands its operations.

The startup uses AI agents to manage high volumes of customer service inquiries for businesses. It differentiates itself through a per-conversation pricing model rather than charging clients per employee seat, a departure from traditional customer service software approaches.

cards.headline: Commodore launches flip phone that blocks social media and browsers
cards.teaser: The Call Back 8020 targets users seeking reduced screen time without fully abandoning mobile connectivity.
cards.body:

Commodore introduced the Call Back 8020, a flip phone designed to restrict access to social media platforms and web browsers. The company, which resurrected the iconic 1980s computer brand, markets the device as a tool for users wanting to reduce digital distractions.

The phone represents Commodore's entry into the mobile device market after previously focusing on computing products. The Call Back 8020 joins a growing category of simplified phones aimed at consumers seeking alternatives to smartphones with full internet access.

hero.headline: Serena and Venus Williams receive Wimbledon doubles wildcard
hero.body:
Serena Williams has been granted a wildcard to play women's doubles at Wimbledon alongside her sister Venus, marking a significant comeback for the tennis legend. The All England Club announced the wildcard recipients on Tuesday morning, with the decision generating considerable attention due to Serena's return to competitive tennis after four years away from the sport.

Serena, a seven-time singles champion, did not request a singles wildcard and has been unclear about whether she plans to compete in the singles draw. At 44 years old, she is focusing on doubles competition. Venus, a five-time singles champion, also did not receive a singles wildcard. The 46-year-old has remained active on the professional tour since her debut in 1994, taking breaks only due to health concerns.

The Williams sisters represent one of the most successful doubles partnerships in tennis history. Together, they have won 14 Grand Slam doubles titles, the joint-second highest in the open era. At Wimbledon specifically, they have claimed six women's doubles titles, the highest achievement in the open era at that venue. The pair has also won three Olympic gold medals in women's doubles and reached number one in the WTA rankings.

Beyond the Williams sisters, the All England Club made several other notable wildcard announcements. Maja Chwalinska, who reached the French Open women's singles final as a qualifier, received a wildcard despite falling outside the rankings cutoff. Her sharp ranking rise to number 21 gives her the rare status of being both a wildcard and seeded player at a Grand Slam tournament.

Singles wildcards were awarded to veterans Stan Wawrinka, who will retire this year, and Grigor Dimitrov. Britain's Dan Evans, retiring after the Championships, did not receive a singles wildcard but was granted entry into the men's doubles alongside compatriot Henry Searle.

Serena has already begun her comeback campaign on the grass court season. She won her first match at Queen's Club with partner Victoria Mboko against Routliffe and Melichar Martinez. However, Mboko subsequently withdrew from the remainder of the grass season after suffering a medial collateral ligament injury. Serena continued her comeback by competing with Karolina Muchova, ranked number 10 in singles, in a Berlin WTA tournament match.

The wildcard system allows tournament organizers to grant entry to players who might not otherwise qualify based on current rankings but possess significant drawing power or face special circumstances. The decision to grant the Williams sisters entry into the doubles draw represents recognition of both their historical dominance in the sport and the considerable interest their return generates among tennis fans worldwide.

cards.headline: Tunisia fires coach Sabri Lamouchi after one World Cup match
cards.teaser: Tunisia dismissed manager Sabri Lamouchi after just one game at the World Cup and appointed former Morocco coach Herve Renard as his replacement.
cards.body:
Tunisia sacked head coach Sabri Lamouchi after just one match at the World Cup. The swift decision represented one of the tournament's quickest managerial changes.

Hervé Renard, who previously managed Morocco and Saudi Arabia, was appointed as Lamouchi's replacement. Renard brings extensive experience from leading national teams at major competitions.

cards.headline: England defender Tino Livramento faces World Cup injury doubt
cards.teaser: England defender Tino Livramento suffered an injury that could rule him out of the World Cup campaign ahead of the team's opening match.
cards.body:
Tino Livramento's participation in England's World Cup campaign is in serious doubt after the defender suffered an injury on the eve of the tournament. The setback comes at a critical time as the Three Lions prepare to begin their competition.

The injury represents a significant concern for England manager Thomas Tuchel's defensive setup, with Livramento having been expected to feature in the squad before the late fitness issue emerged.

cards.headline: Tuchel's England contract includes performance requirements
cards.teaser: England manager Thomas Tuchel signed a contract extension that contains a performance clause tied to results.
cards.body:
Thomas Tuchel's new contract with England includes performance-based conditions, according to FA chief executive Mark Bullingham. The extension ties the manager's future to achieving specific results with the national team.

The clause structure represents a shift in how the Football Association structures managerial contracts. Bullingham confirmed the performance requirements as part of the agreement that keeps Tuchel in charge of the Three Lions.

cards.headline: Iranian team says it was forced to leave United States after World Cup match
cards.teaser: Iran's national team claimed it had to return to Mexico immediately following its opening World Cup match against New Zealand in the United States.
cards.body:
The Iranian national team stated it was required to depart the United States right after playing its first World Cup game. The team drew with New Zealand before reportedly being told to leave American territory and return to Mexico.

Iran's coach described the team as the most oppressed at the World Cup and said FIFA president Gianni Infantino promised to help address the situation. The team criticized the tournament organization over the travel arrangements and restrictions placed on their movements during the competition.

cards.headline: Ghana challenges Canada's visa denial for midfielder Thomas Partey
cards.teaser: Ghana's government filed for a legal review after Canada refused to grant a visa to midfielder Thomas Partey.
cards.body:
Ghana's government has filed for a judicial review of Canada's decision to deny midfielder Thomas Partey a visa. The case is set to be heard in Canadian court as Ghana seeks to overturn the refusal.

The visa denial prevents Partey from participating in matches scheduled to take place in Canada.

cards.headline: Iraq player Zidane Iqbal to make World Cup history for Pakistan heritage
cards.teaser: Former Manchester United player Zidane Iqbal will become the first player of Pakistani heritage to appear at a men's World Cup when he plays for Iraq.
cards.body:
Zidane Iqbal is set to make history at the World Cup as the first player of Pakistani heritage to feature in the men's tournament. The midfielder will compete for Iraq at the competition.

Iqbal is a former Manchester United player who has transitioned to international football with Iraq, achieving this historic milestone for representation of Pakistani heritage on football's biggest stage.

hero.headline: Brian Cox to Receive Icon Award at Raindance Film Festival
hero.body:
The Raindance Film Festival announced it will present a Raindance Icon Award to Golden Globe-winning actor Brian Cox ahead of the festival's 34th edition opening in London. The Scottish actor, known for his role in the television series Succession, joins a group of honorees at this year's event.

Cox will be recognized alongside fellow award recipients Miriam Margolyes and studio head Lloyd Kaufman. The late American musician Eddie Cochran is also set to receive recognition at the festival. The awards ceremony represents part of the festival's tradition of honoring significant figures in film and entertainment.

The Raindance Film Festival has built a reputation as a platform for independent filmmakers and established talent since its founding. The Icon Award specifically recognizes individuals who have made substantial contributions to the film industry through their body of work. Cox's career spans decades across film, television, and theater, with notable performances in projects ranging from stage productions to major television dramas.

The festival opens its 34th edition in London, continuing its role as one of the United Kingdom's prominent independent film festivals. Raindance has historically served as a venue for emerging filmmakers alongside established industry figures. The event typically features film screenings, workshops, and industry panels in addition to its awards presentations.

Cox's recognition comes at a time when his profile has reached new heights following his performance in Succession, which earned him a Golden Globe. The Icon Award adds to his list of accolades accumulated over a career that has included work across multiple mediums and genres. The festival's opening follows the tradition of beginning with recognition of both emerging and established talent in the film industry.

cards.headline: Raindance Film Festival Opens 34th Edition in London
cards.teaser: The Raindance Film Festival begins its 34th edition in London with multiple award presentations planned.
cards.body:
The Raindance Film Festival announced a slate of award recipients as it prepares to open its 34th edition in London. The festival will honor multiple figures from the entertainment industry, including actors Miriam Margolyes and Brian Cox, studio head Lloyd Kaufman, and late musician Eddie Cochran.

The festival continues its tradition of recognizing both emerging and established talent across film and entertainment. Raindance has maintained its position as a prominent independent film festival in the United Kingdom since its founding.

cards.headline: YouTube Expands Presence at Mipcom Television Market
cards.teaser: YouTube will feature an opening day keynote and daily workshops at Mipcom in October after debuting at the event in 2025.
cards.body:
YouTube announced an expanded presence at Mipcom in Cannes this October, building on its debut appearance at the television market in 2025. The platform will deliver an opening day keynote from Pedro Pina and host daily workshops and panels throughout the event.

The company described the expanded presence as an effort to position YouTube as a core distribution and monetization platform for television content. The move reflects the platform's increasing focus on the traditional television industry and its role in content distribution.

cards.headline: British Actor Matthew Broome Expresses Interest in James Bond Role
cards.teaser: Rising actor Matthew Broome, star of The Buccaneers and My Fault: London, said he would welcome the opportunity to audition for the next Bond film.
cards.body:
British actor Matthew Broome has expressed enthusiasm about auditioning for the next James Bond film. Currently starring in Apple TV's The Buccaneers and the My Fault: London franchise on Prime Video, Broome will receive the International Golden Nymph for Most Promising Talent at an upcoming ceremony.

When discussing his career prospects, Broome said he would welcome the opportunity to audition for the iconic spy role, despite uncertainty about his next professional project.

cards.headline: Canadian Animator Cordell Barker Producing Christmas Special
cards.teaser: Two-time Oscar-nominated animator Cordell Barker is producing The Anta Claus of the South Pole, scheduled for release in 2026.
cards.body:
Canadian animator Cordell Barker is producing "The Anta Claus of the South Pole," an alternative Christmas special set for release in 2026. Barker is known for creating the Oscar-nominated short films "The Cat Came Back" and "Strange Invaders."

The project is a co-production involving Tonic DNA and the National Film Board of Canada, made in association with Crave, a division of Bell Media Inc.

cards.headline: Verizon Reunites Austin Powers and Ugly Betty Casts for Ad Campaign
cards.teaser: Verizon brought together the original casts of Austin Powers and Ugly Betty to promote its new Simplicity Plan.
cards.body:
Verizon launched a promotional campaign featuring reunited casts from Austin Powers and the original Ugly Betty to advertise its new Simplicity Plan. The telecommunications company plans to eliminate activation and upgrade fees for customers who have already paid for phone service.

The Simplicity Plan includes new promotions that offer returns on dollars spent. Verizon is using the nostalgic appeal of the two entertainment properties to draw attention to the changes in its service offerings and fee structure.

cards.headline: Steven Knight Credits BBC for Peaky Blinders Creation
cards.teaser: Peaky Blinders creator Steven Knight told a House of Commons inquiry the show would not have been made without the BBC.
cards.body:
Steven Knight, creator of Peaky Blinders, has stated the show would never have been made without the BBC's support. While acknowledging the broadcaster operates with tight budgets compared to other networks and streaming platforms, Knight emphasized its crucial role in enabling productions that might struggle to secure funding elsewhere.

Knight made these comments during a House of Commons inquiry into the BBC's future. His testimony highlighted the public broadcaster's distinct value in the media landscape, despite its financial constraints.

hero.headline: FBI stops potential explosive drone attack on White House UFC event
hero.body:
Federal authorities disrupted a potential attack targeting the UFC Freedom 250 event at the White House, FBI Director Kash Patel announced Tuesday. The operation spanned multiple states and resulted in several arrests.

Law enforcement first learned of the threat on June 10 through encrypted communications on Signal, just days before the sporting event took place on the White House South Lawn. Patel's statement confirmed that the plot involved explosive-laden drones aimed at the outdoor UFC competition.

The Secret Service and FBI coordinated the security response across multiple jurisdictions to track down those allegedly involved in planning the attack. Federal agents monitoring encrypted messaging detected discussions about the potential threat and moved quickly to identify and apprehend suspects before the event occurred.

Patel did not provide specific numbers of arrests or identify the individuals involved in the alleged plot. The investigation did not disclose whether authorities seized any actual explosives or drones, or what additional security measures were implemented at the White House after the threat was discovered.

The UFC Freedom 250 event marked an unusual use of the White House grounds, which are traditionally reserved for state dinners, diplomatic ceremonies, and ceremonial events. The competition drew thousands of attendees to the South Lawn, one of the most heavily protected sites in the United States.

The incident highlights security challenges posed by large public gatherings at sensitive government locations. The discovery of the threat raises questions about how federal agencies monitor and respond to potential dangers targeting major events held at the nation's capital.

Dana White, the UFC's president, later stated the White House event would be a one-time occurrence. He cited weather concerns, the logistical complexity of constructing a cage and staging infrastructure at a federal landmark, and the substantial costs associated with holding the event at the presidential residence as reasons why such events would not be repeated.

The successful interdiction demonstrates the ongoing role of encrypted message monitoring in detecting potential threats to major public events. The operation reflects broader security protocols for protecting high-profile gatherings, particularly those held at locations with symbolic and strategic importance to the federal government.

The incident occurred amid a broader period of scrutiny over security protocols and threat detection at sensitive venues. While details about the specific nature of the threat and those arrested remain limited, the operation underscores the coordination required between multiple federal agencies to protect events drawing large crowds to prominent government sites.

cards.headline: Senate Republicans demand more details on Trump Iran peace deal
cards.teaser: Republican senators are holding back from endorsing the announced peace agreement with Iran, saying they need more information about whether it stops Iran's nuclear program.
cards.body:
Republican senators are withholding judgment on President Trump's announced Iran peace deal, saying they need additional information before weighing in. Members from both parties agreed that Congress must receive more details soon.

Trump's allies on Capitol Hill want clarity on whether the agreement would curb Iran's nuclear program, citing concerns that prompted U.S. and Israeli strikes against Iran earlier this year. Senators are seeking assurances that any deal addresses the core issues that led to the military action.

cards.headline: Trump endorses Collins in Georgia Senate runoff against Dooley
cards.teaser: President Trump made a last-minute endorsement backing Rep. Mike Collins in the Georgia Republican primary runoff, setting up a showdown with Gov. Brian Kemp.
cards.body:
President Trump endorsed Rep. Mike Collins over the weekend in the Georgia Republican primary runoff for Senate, where voters head to the polls Tuesday. The contest pits Collins against former college football coach Derek Dooley, who has the backing of Gov. Brian Kemp.

The race tests Trump's endorsement power against Kemp's influence in Georgia. Collins faces the winner in a general election matchup against Sen. Jon Ossoff. Alabama also holds a Republican Senate primary runoff Tuesday, offering another measure of Trump's sway with voters in the party.

cards.headline: Anthropic pulls AI models after White House export control order
cards.teaser: The Trump administration directed Anthropic to disable its newest AI models, prompting warnings that ad hoc regulation could hurt innovation.
cards.body:
Anthropic disabled its Fable 5 and Mythos 5 models after receiving a federal export control directive requiring the company to block foreign nationals from accessing them. The order, issued by the Trump administration on national security grounds, prompted Anthropic to suspend the models for all users rather than implement selective access restrictions.

The move has drawn criticism from AI policy advocates who say the administration's approach lacks transparency and clear guidelines. The company stated it received no specific details about the national security concerns underlying the directive, raising questions about how tech companies can comply with unpredictable regulatory demands while maintaining operational stability.

cards.headline: US Ebola response lags as outbreak spreads
cards.teaser: The United States, once a pioneer in fighting infectious disease worldwide, is now playing catch-up with a deadly Ebola outbreak.
cards.body:
The United States is now playing catch-up with a deadly Ebola outbreak, marking a shift for a country once considered a pioneer in the worldwide fight against infectious disease. The lag in response comes as the outbreak continues to spread.

The American role in global health has diminished as other nations and organizations step forward to address the crisis. The question of who will lead international efforts to contain the outbreak remains unclear as the US takes a more reactive posture than in past public health emergencies.

cards.headline: Democrats search for next party leader ahead of 2028 race
cards.teaser: As Democrats celebrate the opening of the Obama Presidential Center in Chicago, party members are asking who will emerge as the next Barack Obama.
cards.body:
Democrats gathering this week for the opening of the Obama Presidential Center in Chicago are confronting a question that has loomed over the party since the former president left office nearly a decade ago: Who is the next Barack Obama? The answer remains elusive.

In 2008, Obama energized voters with his message and campaign style, setting a standard the party has struggled to replicate. As Democrats look toward the 2028 presidential race, the search for a candidate who can match Obama's political appeal continues without a clear frontrunner emerging from the field.

cards.headline: Iran war could reshape Republican standing with voters
cards.teaser: The brief U.S.-Iran war stands to have larger consequences for the GOP with voters, though the truce scheduled for Friday has not yet been finalized.
cards.body:
The brief war between the United States and Iran could carry significant consequences for Republicans with voters, even as questions remain about whether the truce will hold. President Trump and Iranian leaders are known for unpredictable negotiating styles, leaving uncertainty about whether the agreement will be signed Friday as announced.

Assuming the deal holds, the conflict will be remembered as brief, but its political impact on the Republican Party may extend well beyond the short duration of hostilities. The outcome of negotiations and the terms of any final agreement will shape how voters assess the administration's handling of the crisis.
